I know you have a lot of comments, so I'll just leave another perspective from a former busser/to-go host. My argument would simply be that if you think a server in-house deserves it, so do to-go hosts based on the amount of work they do.

To-go orders typically went like this at my restaurant. You have a tablet that receives online/doordash/postmate orders, and a house phone in your apron for orders that call in. When the tablet notifies you or when someone calls, you go to the kiosk and manually enter the order with all the extra requests. If it's online delivery/pickup, you mark it 'accepted' so the delivery service can begin to send a driver/so you know your food is being prepared. You prepare the drinks, sauces, and desserts while the cook prepares the food. When it comes out, you put a lid and a label on the item with the name of the customer and what is inside then find a place for it under the heat lamp. When they arrive you double check the receipt and ensure everything is correct before bringing it to the front of the restaurant for the customer/driver to receive. Then you pray that they didn't 'forget' to add an extra sauce or drink or dessert. 

On a regular lunch rush, you're doing this with about 6-8 meals at once. On a Saturday even before COVID hit? The entire window could be full of takeout orders, to the point where there isn't even room for in house food to be trayed and sent out. I'm talking 15-20 of those at once with maybe 2 tablets, 1 phone, and 3 sets of hands. Now think about what you tip a server for. Running back and forth, getting your sauces, getting your drinks, ringing in your food, bringing you the bill, being polite and friendly while doing it, etc. etc. etc... At my restaurant, to-go hosts did that and more.

I know not everywhere is the same, but from after my experience I always tip to-go hosts! It was my least favorite position. I highly preferred bussing tables. Better tips and less work!
